transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Martin Chu (Halcyon CTO), Sana Patel (Head of Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Legal)

Summary:
Halcyon Health is advancing through procurement. Main topics: redline of MSA/DPA, SLA targets for hosted vs dedicated, data residency and KMS requirements, SOC2/ISO evidence, pricing (committed vs usage), pilot scope and timeline. Redwood AE+SE clarified hosting options and next steps for redlines, security docs, and performance benchmarks.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA terms
- SLA and uptime/latency targets for critical routes
- Data residency, encryption, KMS/HSM integration
- Pilot scope, benchmarks, pricing model
- Procurement timeline and decision owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan Kim here, AE at Redwood. We got Priya on the call from our engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Martin (Halcyon): Doing well, thanks. Sana and Liam are on with me. We wanted to move the MSA/DPA along - procurement's pushing to close by end of month if possible.
[00:12] Sana (Halcyon): Yep, timeline is aggressive, we've got a board milestone end of June so if we can align on legal and pricing that helps.
[00:18] Jordan: Totally; we'll do our best. Priya, do you want to run through the hosting options and SLA guarantees so legal/procurement have the context?
[00:24] Priya (Redwood): Sure. So, Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/VPC deployments. For enterprise we'll typically offer a dedicated pool with SLA-backed latency and uptime - e.g., 99.95% uptime on dedicated with latency SLOs per model class. Hosted plan has slightly lower SLA and best-effort latency but faster onboarding. Important note: we have automatic fallback routing so if dedicated capacity is constrained requests can fall back to a compatible variant; that's configurable per-customer.
[00:44] Liam (Halcyon): On the fallback, does data ever leave the region? Our data residency policy requires EU-only processing for EU customers.
[00:50] Priya: Good question - we can pin routing by region and account for residency. For EU workloads we can lock to EU regions and avoid cross-region fallback. There is a note though that in some extreme failover scenarios we escalate - but we can write the routing policy restriction into the DPA/SLA.
[01:04] Martin: Okay. On encryption, we need KMS/HSM integration and that logs access events to our SIEM. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[01:11] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS - AWS KMS or customer HSMs for our private deployments. For hosted accounts we can integrate with your KMS using a customer-managed key and provide audit logs for key usage. (audio: slight echo)
[01:25] Sana: Excellent, that's a big checkbox. Liam, any initial redline hotspots?
[01:28] Liam: A few. Liability cap language, data deletion timelines in the DPA, and audit access - we want a 30 day SOC2 review window and rights to audit with reasonable notice. Also indemnity carve-outs for regulated data.
[01:40] Jordan: Understood. For liability we typically negotiate a multiple of fees or a fixed cap; happy to discuss. On audit, we can provide SOC2 Type II and ISO docs - Priya will share the latest artifacts.
[01:52] Priya: I'll upload SOC2 and ISO certs after the call; I'll also include a network architecture diagram and our incident response playbook redacted for customer privacy.
[01:59] Martin: When you say SOC2, do you provide the full report or a bridge letter? Procurement usually wants the full report under an NDA.
[02:05] Priya: We can provide the SOC2 Type II report under an NDA. We usually deliver via secure link and can do a one-time view/download.
[02:12] Sana: Great. Pricing - can we talk committed usage discounts vs pay-as-you-go? Our finance team prefers predictable monthly commits.
[02:19] Jordan: Sure. We have usage-based pricing for hosted API, and reserved capacity for Dedicated with discounts based on commit and term length (monthly/annual). Typical committed discounts are 20-35% depending on GPU class, model profile, and volume. We can run a model-specific quote once we have your token volume estimates.
[02:36] Martin: Our initial estimate is 50M tokens/month for the pilot, ramping to 200M in 6 months. Does that align with reserved capacity tiers?
[02:43] Jordan: Yes, that's a typical enterprise pilot. We'll map that to a dedicated pod size and provide per-token economics. For the pilot we can offer a short-term reserved burst with an option to convert to annual commit.
[02:55] Liam: SLA specifics - we need objective latency SLOs for our critical inference route (model: rwd-instruct-11b). What numbers can you commit to?
[03:03] Priya: For a model in that class on dedicated with 8-GPU pod, 95th percentile p95 tail latency for a 2k token response should be below 800ms under normal load. We'll include exact benchmarks in the performance sheet. For hosted the p95 can vary; we'll give you both numbers and the test harness we used.
[03:23] Martin: Can you put the exact test harness and seed prompts so we can reproduce? We want reproducibility.
[03:28] Priya: Absolutely - we'll share the harness, sequence length distribution, and the KV/prefix caching settings used. Note, our runtime uses KV cache and continuous batching; sometimes transcriptions call that 'kay vee cache' in notes ;)
[03:41] Sana: On the DPA, data retention and deletion timelines are critical. We want a guaranteed 7-day data retention max for logs and request payloads, unless we agree otherwise for debugging.
[03:50] Priya: For hosted we retain logs for 30 days by default, but we can negotiate retention windows in the DPA to 7 days for payloads with an SLA for purge. For private deployments retention is under customer control.
[04:03] Liam: Need explicit language for deletion and certification of deletion.
[04:07] Jordan: We can add deletion attestation language and an export path for data.
[04:10] [05:00] Speaker 2 (Redwood): mm-hmm, just to add, incident response window for P1 is 1 hour and for P2 is 4 hours for dedicated customers under our SLA.
[05:12] Liam: That's helpful. We also need an escalation matrix to be included as an appendix to the SLA.
[05:18] Jordan: We'll include the escalation contacts and on-call procedure.
[05:22] Martin: One more on compliance: do you support encryption in transit with customer cert pinning? Some of our partners require mTLS.
[05:29] Priya: We support TLS1.2/1.3; mTLS can be accommodated on private deployments and dedicated VPC endpoints. For hosted we can do per-customer TLS termination with custom certs in some plans.
[05:40] Sana: Okay. Let's talk about legal redlines - I'll share Halcyon's standard procurement template after the call. Liam will flag top three must-haves. Jordan, can you commit to returning a redline within 3 business days?
[05:52] Jordan: Yes, we'll aim for a 3 business day turnaround for initial redline.
[05:56] Liam: Expect us to push back on indemnity and data breach notification windows.
[06:01] Jordan: Understood.
[06:05] [10:00] Jordan: On onboarding logistics - we'll need an onboarding call with your engineering team to provision test keys, and a pilot runbook. Priya will lead the technical onboarding.
[10:12] Priya: For the pilot, suggested scope: 2-week technical validation, 50M tokens, test harness runs for latency and throughput, and a customer success check-in at day 10. We can do a short canary for production routing if you want.
[10:26] Martin: Sounds good. Who from Redwood will be the single point of contact for technical blockers?
[10:30] Priya: That's me - priya@redwood.com and I'll add an on-call slack channel during pilot.
[10:36] Sana: For procurement, we'll need a final pricing sheet that lists committed vs on-demand and what happens for overages. Also, clear termination/exit terms (data export, handover).
[10:45] Jordan: We'll include an overage calc and a 30/60/90 day exit process in the MSA appendix.
[10:50] Liam: On indemnity, we may ask to exclude regulatory fines for willful misconduct; want to see Redwood's position on that.
[10:57] Jordan: We can discuss carve-outs - we'll come back with our standard language and highlight negotiable items.
[11:02] [20:00] Martin: Performance benchmarks - will you provide both hosted and dedicated numbers in the sheet? We need p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
[20:08] Priya: Yes, we'll provide p50/p95/p99, throughput at different batch sizes, and notes on quantization/latency tradeoffs. We'll also include guidance on model variants and fallback behavior.
[20:18] Martin: Good. Also, can you include a note on cost optimization levers - batching, caching, quantization profiles? Finance wants to understand unit economics.
[20:25] Jordan: Already on the list. Redwood Optimize recommendations will be in the ops appendix.
[20:29] Sana: About procurement approvals - our legal wants the DPA perfect before finance signs. So timeline is legal sign-off -> finance PO -> exec approval. We're aiming to have legal review done by 6/24. Are Redwood timelines compatible?
[20:40] Jordan: Yes, if we get your redlines this week we'll be able to turn around by 6/18 and support your 6/24 legal sign-off.
[20:46] Liam: Note - we'll likely require an SLA credit schedule with an explicit service credit calculation for downtime.
[20:51] Priya: We'll provide a credit schedule; it's usually a percentage of monthly fees per downtime bucket.
[20:55] Martin: For the pilot, do you allow data to be scoped to our dev environment only? We don't want production data hitting test endpoints.
[21:02] Priya: Yes - test keys and separate environments for dev/pilot/prod. We'll ensure separation at the tenancy level.
[21:08] [30:00] Jordan: Quick question - any blockers on your side for receiving SOC2 or environment diagrams?
[30:06] Sana: No, that's fine. Liam will focus on redlines. We do want a sample DPA that has explicit subprocessor lists.
[30:13] Priya: We'll include the current subprocessor list and a clause for notification on new subprocessors with 30 day notice.
[30:20] Liam: That notice period is required, yes.
[30:24] Martin: On pricing again, if we commit to annual reserved capacity, can we get a price lock for 12 months?
[30:31] Jordan: Yes, price lock available for the committed term; annual commits generally get deeper discounts and a 12-month lock.
[30:37] Sana: Ok. Let's align on dates: Halcyon will send redlines by EOD 6/16. Jordan will return redline by 6/18. Priya will share SOC2/ISO and performance sheet by 6/15. Then we reconvene for pricing finalization the week of 6/22.
[30:52] Jordan: Sounds like a plan. Anything else?
[30:55] Martin: One risk - we have a vendor that promised on-prem, but they'd require us to run ops. We prefer Redwood if you can meet our security asks.
[31:04] Jordan: We'll highlight the Private option and managed on-prem if needed, but most customers go Dedicated or Private VPC. We'll put the differences in the onboarding doc.
[31:12] Liam: Also want to confirm retention of logs for debugging - if we agree to 7 days for payloads, do you retain aggregated metrics longer?
[31:20] Priya: Aggregated metrics we can retain longer for monitoring, but payloads and PII can be set to shorter windows. We'll capture that in the DPA.
[31:28] Sana: Great. If that's all, we'll stop recording and get the redline out.
[31:33] Jordan: Thanks everyone - next steps captured. We'll send the redline and security artifacts.
[31:38] [End of recording]
